All five states are reachable_from_initial=true, every state has outgoing transitions (no leaf/deadlock frontier), and all five declared events have a reachable consumer transition, so NL1-ELEMENT-1 (element_declaration, satisfied by ClampingState/BrakingState presence), NL2-INITENTRY-1 (InitialState->BrakingState exists at transition:line:12), NL2-ENDPOINT-1 (InitialState->OperationalState exists at transition:line:13), NL2-ENDPOINT-2 (BrakingState->InitialState exists at transition:line:16), NL3-ENDPOINT-1 (BrakingState->ClampingState exists at transition:line:14), the derived containment (ClampingState is a direct child state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0051 sibling of BrakingState, same scope), and the derived event_consumption for Brake_Signal_Received (reachable consumer InitialState/transition:line:12) are all satisfied and omitted. The behavioral consequence issue this lens surfaces is guard_disjointness (NL2-DISJOINT-1): the two braking-state alternatives (transmission-fails-guarded exit to OperationalState vs feedback-sent event to InitialState) are modeled with mismatched carriers - the NL binds the transmission-failure branch to BrakingState but the FCSTM only has InitialState->OperationalState on Signal_Transmission_Fails, so BrakingState's two actual outgoing edges (ClampingState via Entering_Clamping_State, InitialState via Signal_Feedback_Sent) are only trigger-distinguished by event names with no guard field populated anywhere (guard=null on every transition), leaving the guard-disjointness property predicate-null/unsupported. I also inspect termination-like continuation: ClampingState routes back to InitialState (not a designated completion state per NL, so no termination contract applies) and OperationalState also returns to InitialState, both preserving cyclic operational continuation rather than a dead end, which is consistent with no deadlock_freedom obligation being stated in NL, so no V1 candidate is warranted.
